facts.fact: The San Joaquin Marsh, about 300 acres of restored ponds and wetland in the flood plain of San Diego Creek, lies just west of the course (OSM: the Ponds 1-6 and A-E beside the course boundary).
The American avocet is photographed at the UC San Joaquin Marsh Reserve, a ten-minute walk from UC Irvine.
The course has lakes in play (three or four by different accounts).

concepts.name: The Marsh Avocet
concepts.rationale: An American avocet in breeding colours (cinnamon head and neck, black-and-white back, long upturned bill, blue-grey legs) wading in a pond: the bird of the marsh next door, and the course's own lakes.
concepts.symbolism: The marsh and the lakes; a shorebird not used by any other course in the game (Oregon Golf Club has a great blue heron, Bandon Preserve a snowy plover).
concepts.interpretation: The choice of bird is the course chat's; nothing says the club uses it. The club's own logo was not looked at (its site is not reachable from the sandbox); an avocet is not a known mark of the club.
concepts.strengths: The upturned bill and the cinnamon head read at 32 px; it says marsh and Southern California water birds.
concepts.tradeoffs: A wading bird is close in kind to Oregon Golf Club's heron; the colours and the bill keep it distinct.

recommendation: Concept 1 (the only one drawn; overnight build, the developer's permission to design the logo).
